name: bash
description: Run a shell command in the workspace root. Output is truncated if long. A command still running when its foreground window elapses is NOT killed — it converts to background work: you get a handle immediately and the full result arrives as a message, so a slow build or test suite always completes. Use this for running commands (builds, tests, git); when a dedicated tool fits, prefer it over the bash equivalent — grep/glob/keyword_search to search, read_file to read — they stay inside the workspace boundary and give better results. Never use `find` or `grep -r` to search a repository: they crawl node_modules/vendor/.git and can run for minutes on a large monorepo, while the built-in glob/grep/keyword_search skip those trees. There is no TTY: interactive commands (`git rebase -i`, editors, REPLs, prompts) hang until killed. Do not commit, push, or create branches unless the user asks.

timeout_s.description: Foreground window override for this call, in seconds (clamped to [1, 3600]). The call blocks your turn at most this long; if the command is still running when it elapses, it converts to background work and the result arrives as a message. Set it when you know the command's cost: higher to wait synchronously for a known-slow command whose result you need before deciding anything, lower to bail out fast on something that might hang.

background.description: Run the command in the background from the start: returns a work handle immediately; the result arrives as a message when it finishes. Prefer this over timeout_s for commands you already know are long (full test suites, installs, builds).

notify.description: For background work only: when its outcome flows back to you as a message. 'always' (default), 'on_fail' (only when it fails), or 'none' (fire-and-forget: no message, the result is not retrievable — use only when you genuinely do not need the outcome).
